title: Compute brief - 20 October 2026
description: Grid access is turning from a queue into a price. Google funds about $600 million of Entergy Arkansas grid and storage plus a 440 MW solar PPA for West Memphis; Denmark puts data centres last for constrained grid capacity; Israel proposes a 200 MW cap per new data center with NIS 2 million per MW guarantees. Tape: 71 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Tenants pay for the grid; Denmark and Israel ration it
lede: Two answers to the same grid constraint landed between Sunday and Monday. In Arkansas the tenant pays: Entergy Arkansas announced a second phase of service for Google's West Memphis campus, with Google covering about $600 million of battery, substation and transmission investment plus a 440 MW solar PPA, pending Arkansas PSC approval and an expected 2028 in-service date. Where no tenant pays, governments ration: Denmark's executive order 892 took effect on 19 October and places data centres in the lowest of four priority categories when grid capacity is short, and Israel's Electricity Authority backed a 200 MW cap per new data center, about 1,000 MW of new large connections and NIS 2 million per MW guarantees after 27,000 MW of requests. Goldman Sachs counts 86 data center projects canceled or significantly delayed since January, 76 of them tied to local opposition, and calls power 'probably the forever bottleneck'. Capital is still chasing sites with power: Bloomberg and CNBC report Anthropic is in talks for a second 460 MW building at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia worth about $45 billion, even as investors push back on Nscale's roughly $30 billion IPO target and Korea's Elice fell about 30% on its KOSDAQ debut. On the public silicon tape all six venues returned HTTP 200: 71 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW. CoreWeave's list held at $6.16 for H100 even as Goldman's upgrade note cites CoreWeave price increases of 25% in July and 10% in October, which sit in contracts, not the public page.

countries.name: United States
countries.note: Entergy Arkansas phase 2 for Google West Memphis: Google covers about $600 million of batteries (1,400 MWh), substation and two 230 kV lines plus a 440 MW solar PPA; APSC approval pending, 2028 in service (Wire, 19 Oct). Anthropic in talks for a second 460 MW Nscale Monarch building in West Virginia, about $45 billion (Signal).

countries.name: Denmark
countries.note: Executive order 892 in force 19 Oct: data centres are category 4 of 4 for constrained grid capacity; operators can refuse requests that displace higher priorities; 3 MW+ requests handled in regional rounds at least twice a year (Wire).

countries.name: Israel
countries.note: Electricity Authority backs a 200 MW cap per new data center, about 1,000 MW of new large-DC connections on top of about 2,000 MW approved, NIS 2 million per MW guarantees; 27,000 MW was requested; three-week consultation next (Wire, 18 Oct).

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.note: Aolani signs non-binding LOIs for up to 500 MW of AI data centre capacity from 2H 2027; projects up to 580 MW committed in Malaysia by 2027 versus about 80 MW in 2026 (Wire, 19 Oct).

silicon.name: H100 HGX

watch.name: NextDC M3 announcement
watch.note: No update yet at our cutoff; the halt ends with an announcement or at the 21 Oct open (about 4 pm PT on 20 Oct). Watch the stated cause, MW affected, delay length and any FY27 guidance change.

watch.name: Anthropic / Nscale Monarch building 2
watch.note: Bloomberg says a deal for a second 460 MW Vera Rubin building, about $45 billion, could be signed within days; Anthropic would hold a right of first refusal on a third building. Talks only; both declined to comment.

watch.name: Nscale IPO
watch.note: Some investors argue for $16 to 19 billion versus a roughly $30 billion target (Bloomberg via Quartz); marketing on hold while SEC comments are addressed; Norway site reported six months late.

watch.name: Israel data center rules
watch.note: Full decision due for a three-week public consultation; watch whether the 200 MW cap, the 1,000 MW allocation and the NIS 2 million per MW guarantee survive.

watch.name: Meta Q3 results (21 Oct, after close)
watch.note: First hyperscaler print of the season; watch 2026 and 2027 capex guidance and any lease or financing commentary. Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon follow.

watch.note: MEED reports an EPC tender worth about $1 billion for a 100 MW Al-Saad facility (expandable to 200 MW), bids due 8 Nov; tender only.
